summary: This work develops analytical quantum full-wave solutions for single- and two-photon transport through a rectangular waveguide cavity containing a transmon qubit coupled to two coaxial ports using quantum input-output theory. The analysis reveals dramatically different photon scattering signatures between single- and two-photon regimes across the good and bad cavity limits of cavity QED.
motivation: Validating numerical full-wave quantum solvers for superconducting quantum interconnects requires analytical solutions for standard component geometries, which are currently lacking for realistic 3D cavity-qubit systems interfaced through external ports.
method: The authors apply quantum input-output theory formalism to derive analytical expressions for scattering matrix elements and second-order correlation functions $g^{(2)}(\tau)$, combining full-wave classical EM calculations (cavity resonance $\omega_c/2\pi = 7.55$ GHz, coaxial decay rates $\kappa/2\pi = 421.5$ kHz) with quantum qubit dynamics for the transmon ($\omega_q/2\pi = 7.55$ GHz).
result: In the good-cavity regime ($g = 15.9$ MHz $> \kappa$), two-photon transmission is suppressed at single-photon dressed frequencies $\lambda_{1,\pm}$ but enhanced at two-photon dressed frequencies $\lambda_{2,\pm} = \omega_c \pm 2g$; in the bad-cavity regime ($g = 269.3$ kHz $< \kappa$), two-photon transmission becomes possible near the cavity resonance where single-photon reflection dominates, manifesting an analog of dipole-induced transparency.
